BLOCKING FINDING.

B1. THE DELIVERABLE ASSERTS A FALSE CLAIM ABOUT ITSELF, AND THE PROOF RECORD CERTIFIES IT.
reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md, in 'A second limitation, found reviewing this document', defines the hole as applying to 'a pull request whose commits touch only `reviews/` and `proof/`', and then states:
    "**This pull request is itself an instance.** A green `lwb-lanes` here is not evidence that anything in this file was reviewed."
The first sentence is FALSE at the reviewed head. This PR's commits do not touch only reviews/ and proof/: TEN of them touch HANDOFF.md --
    git log --format='%h %s' e5f29bf..HEAD -- HANDOFF.md
    -> 7da6f47, a46dd36, 2eb80f8, 16f1f9c, 220c121, a3be81c, bc6874c, 1e622e3, 7be56dd, 8192011
-- and resolve_reviewable_head consequently returns 7da6f47, a commit this PR DOES modify, not the base commit it does not. The degenerate case the paragraph describes is not the case this PR is in.
PROVENANCE, checked rather than assumed: `git log -S` shows the sentence was written in b224d1b, the branch's second commit, when the branch really was reviews/-only and the claim was TRUE. It became false at 8192011, the next commit to touch HANDOFF.md, and has stood unrevisited across roughly twenty commits since -- including 16f1f9c and a46dd36, two commits whose entire stated purpose was correcting false state claims in prose. This is the failure reviews/README.md already names: a statement bound to a branch that then moved underneath it.
IT IS NOT A HARMLESS SLIP, BECAUSE THE PREMISE UNDERSTATES THE HAZARD AND SO OVER-ASSURES EVERY OTHER PULL REQUEST. I measured what actually happens. On a detached copy of the head I replaced reviews/27/dispatch-correction.md's entire contents with a line of nonsense, in a commit touching nothing else, then asked the resolver:
    raw head        -> 442a82cf9a6c5eb4fa8309f6364145050a631839
    reviewable head -> 7da6f47d99c7f32d3e62baf33fd905f668220455   (unchanged)
So a record naming 7da6f47 stays FRESH while the document under review has been replaced by its own negation -- on a PR that is NOT all-records, and that the paragraph's own definition therefore excludes. The document's CONCLUSION is right; its stated PREMISE is both false about itself and too narrow to support that conclusion for anyone else. A maintainer who reads it and reasons 'my PR touches HANDOFF.md, so the gate covers me' reaches the wrong answer, and this probe is the counter-example.
IT IS CARRIED INTO THE PROOF RECORD. proof/43.json's fourth acceptance criterion reads, in part, 'The document says this PR is itself an instance and tells the reader to read the review record rather than trust the green check', with "met": true. The record certifies as met a criterion whose factual premise is false at the head the record was regenerated against.
WHY I BLOCK ON A DOCUMENTATION CLAIM RATHER THAN NOTING IT. This document's own thesis, two sections earlier, is: 'A document written to be exact about provenance asserted a safeguard that does not exist -- the same error class it was correcting, one level up.' The commit that wrote the sentence I am charging is titled 'docs(reviews): the correction document made the same error it corrects'. A PR whose deliverable is exactness about claims, and whose HANDOFF commits are titled 'fix two false PR-state claims', cannot ship a third false state claim inside the deliverable and call the criterion met.
WHAT WOULD CLEAR IT, and it is small -- one paragraph, no mechanism change. State the hazard by its real shape rather than by commit-set shape: the reviewable head is the newest NON-record-only commit, so content living under `reviews/` or `proof/` is never what a record's freshness is pinned to, whether or not the PR also carries commits elsewhere. Then say what is true of this PR specifically -- its reviewable head 7da6f47 is a HANDOFF.md commit, so a record here attests to the HANDOFF changes, and a later reviews/-only edit to this document would not re-stale it -- and correct proof/43.json's fourth criterion to match. That is strictly more useful to a reader than the sentence being replaced.

My first reading was that the document OVERSTATES the hole -- that because this PR touches HANDOFF.md the reviewable head is real, so 'a green lwb-lanes here is not evidence' was alarmist and the paragraph should be softened. That would have been a false accusation against a correct warning, and acting on it would have deleted a true one. I record it because the version I nearly wrote would have made this repository less safe, and because it is the second time in this run that the only thing separating a real finding from a false one was executing the probe rather than trusting the shape of the code.
I also took the cheaper precaution first: I fetched origin/main BEFORE running lwb_check_state_claims.py, precisely so a stale ref could not make me charge a correct document with a false main-SHA claim. It passed either way, but I am not willing to report a claim-check run against a ref I had not refreshed.
